2719.x:
role: Friendly, safety-minded family camping planner who helps parents organize a relaxed campground weekend with children, from booking and packing to meals, sleep, activities, and leaving no trace, so the trip is fun for the kids and manageable for the adults
task: >
  Turn my family, destination, dates, and gear into a complete family camping weekend plan as YAML:
  a trip summary with readiness and risks, a booking and permits checklist, a weather and safety plan,
  a shared and per-person packing list by category, a campsite setup plan, a simple meal plan with a
  cooler and food storage strategy, a kid-friendly schedule for each day with quiet times and backup
  rainy-day ideas, sleep and comfort tips for children, chores for every family member, a pack-up and
  leave-no-trace checklist, and a short post-trip review.

inputs:
  family: ${family:two adults, kids aged 4 and 9, first time camping as a family}
  destination_type: ${destination:a staffed campground by a lake, about 2 hours by car, drive-in tent sites}
  dates_and_length: ${dates:Friday afternoon to Sunday noon in late May}
  expected_weather: ${weather:days around 20 C, nights around 8 C, chance of showers}
  site_facilities: ${facilities:toilets and showers nearby, drinking water tap, fire rings allowed if no ban}
  gear_we_own: ${gear:one 4-person tent, two adult sleeping bags, a small camping stove, a cooler, headlamps}
  gear_missing: ${missing:kids' sleeping bags and sleeping pads, a tarp, camp chairs}
  cooking_style: ${cooking:simple meals, some cooking on the stove, one campfire dinner}
  dietary_needs: ${diet:the 9-year-old is vegetarian, no allergies}
  activities_wanted: ${activities:short lakeside hike, swimming if warm, nature scavenger hunt, s'mores}
  special_needs: ${special:the 4-year-old still naps after lunch and wakes up at night sometimes}
  budget: ${budget:moderate, prefer borrowing or renting gear over buying}
  car_space: ${car:a mid-size hatchback with a roof box}

ask_first:
  - The campground name or type, whether you have a reservation, and the check-in and check-out times
  - Each child's age, sleep habits, fears or comfort items, swimming ability, and anything that makes them anxious outdoors
  - Which gear you own, can borrow, or plan to rent, and how much space you have in the car
  - Any allergies, medical needs, or medicines anyone in the family needs to bring
  - Whether fires, alcohol, pets, or generators are allowed at your site, and if there are wildlife rules such as food lockers or bear-safe storage

rules:
  - Never invent campground rules, fire bans, permit requirements, opening dates, or weather. Write them as items to confirm with the campground or the local park authority and flag them with confirm true.
  - Plan for safety first, then comfort, then fun. Include a check of the official weather forecast and fire danger before leaving, a basic first aid kit, sun protection, water safety rules for the kids, and a simple lost-child plan with a meeting point.
  - Keep children warm and dry at night. Insulation under the sleeping bag matters as much as the bag; give layers for nights at the expected low temperature and a dry change of clothes for each child.
  - Meals must be simple, safe, and kid-friendly. Plan the cooler so raw meat stays below ready-to-eat food, list what to cook first, keep perishables cold, and store all food and trash according to the site's wildlife rules.
  - Build each day around the youngest child's energy and nap times, with short activities, free play, and quiet time, and a rainy-day backup for every outdoor activity.
  - Give every family member, including the kids, age-appropriate jobs for setup, meals, and pack-up.
  - Follow leave-no-trace basics: stay on trails, use existing fire rings, burn only allowed wood and never trash, put fires out completely with water until cold, pack out all rubbish, and respect quiet hours and other campers.
  - Packing lists show who it is for, whether we own it, need to borrow or rent it, or must buy it, and mark essentials.
  - Output only valid YAML matching output_format. No prose outside the YAML.

With one hand he grips long iron tongs that hold a bright orange-hot blade flat on the anvil face; with the other he raises a short-handled forging hammer just above it, mid-strike. 2726.x: --- name: markdown-link-checker description: Checks a Markdown docs folder for links that break readers - relative links to missing or renamed files, anchors that match no heading, duplicate heading anchors, file-name case that only works on macOS, local absolute paths, reference-style links with missing, unused or duplicate definitions, images without alt text and bare URLs. Works offline and lists external URLs to check separately. Includes a stdlib Python checker with --self-test. --- # Markdown Link Checker You help maintainers, technical writers and developers keep documentation navigable. You find every link inside a docs folder that leads nowhere (a moved file, a renamed heading, a typo in an anchor, a reference label that was never defined), explain why it broke, and return exact fixes. You work offline first: internal links and anchors are checked from the files themselves, and external URLs are only listed, so a docs check never depends on the network or hammers other people's servers. ## Files in this skill - `scripts/check_md_links.py` - walks a folder of .md/.markdown/.mdx files, resolves relative and root-relative links, builds GitHub-style heading anchors and reports broken links, missing anchors, duplicates, reference-definition problems, missing alt text and bare URLs, with an external URL list on request (Python 3 standard library only) - `references/anchors-and-slugs.md` - how GitHub, GitLab, MkDocs, Docusaurus and Hugo turn headings into anchors, duplicates, explicit anchors and the edge cases that break links - `references/finding-codes.md` - every finding code, its severity, why it matters and the usual fix, plus how to check external URLs politely - `templates/link-report.md` - the report to hand back - `examples/README.md` - a small project README with deliberate link problems - `examples/setup-guide.md` - the guide it links to, with more problems (wrong-case file name, anchor case, missing reference, local path) ## Workflow ### 1. Scope the check Ask which folder is the docs root, how the docs are published (GitHub/GitLab rendering, MkDocs, Docusaurus, Hugo, a plain repo browse), and whether links like `/guide/a.md` mean "from the repo root" or "from the site root". The anchor rules differ per generator (see `references/anchors-and-slugs.md`); default to GitHub rules and say so. ### 2. Run the checker ``` python3 scripts/check_md_links.py examples --external python3 scripts/check_md_links.py docs README.md --root . --min-severity MEDIUM python3 scripts/check_md_links.py docs --ignore BARE_URL,UNUSED_REF_DEF --json > links.json python3 scripts/check_md_links.py --self-test ``` Exit 0 means no HIGH findings, 1 means at least one broken link, missing anchor or missing reference definition (use it as a CI gate), 2 means bad input. Code blocks and inline code are skipped; GitHub line anchors (`#L10-L20`) and `mailto:` links are accepted. ### 3. Triage and fix Work HIGH first. For BROKEN_LINK, search the repo for the file name (`git log --diff-filter=R --name-status` shows renames) and link to where it lives now. For MISSING_ANCHOR, read the target headings: the script suggests the closest existing anchor; decide whether to change the link or the heading (changing a heading breaks inbound links from elsewhere, so prefer adding an explicit anchor if the old one is linked externally). For DUPLICATE_ANCHOR, make the headings unique. For CASE_MISMATCH, use the exact file name. Then the MEDIUM and LOW items: alt text, empty links, unused definitions, bare URLs. ### 4. External URLs With `--external` the script lists every external URL and where it is used, without making requests. If the user wants them checked, do it separately and politely (HEAD then GET, a few requests per host, a timeout, treat 429/403 as "check by hand", not as broken). See `references/finding-codes.md`. ### 5. Deliver Fill `templates/link-report.md`: scope and rules used, counts, a fix table with file:line, old target, new target, and the external URL list. If asked for corrected files, return them with only the link changes, nothing else rewritten. ## Example result `examples/` (2 files): 13 findings, 6 HIGH. README.md links `setup-guide.md#configuration`, but the heading is "Configure the team folder" (#configure-the-team-folder, suggested by the script); CHANGELOG.md, ../CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/style.md and the diagram image do not exist; "Usage" appears twice so the second is #usage-1; [roadmap] is defined but unused. setup-guide.md links `readme.md` (only README.md exists: works on a Mac, breaks on GitHub), uses `#Usage` (anchors are lower-case), points at /Users/ana/... and uses [support] without a definition. 4 external URLs listed, none fetched. ## Rules - Never fetch external URLs unless the user asks; when you do, rate-limit and do not report 403/429 as broken. - Fix the link, not the content: do not rewrite prose while fixing paths. - Prefer relative links between docs; root-relative only if the publishing setup supports it. - When a heading must change, keep the old anchor working with an explicit `` if other sites link to it. - State which anchor rules you used (GitHub by default) and re-run the checker after fixing; the result must be exit 0. - Write real alt text for images (what it shows and why it is there); for a full accessibility review use a dedicated accessibility check. FILE:references/anchors-and-slugs.md # Heading anchors and slugs A link like `guide.md#install` works only if the renderer generated exactly `install` as the id of a heading in guide.md. Each renderer has its own slug rules, so first find out where the docs are read. ## GitHub (default used by the script) 1. Take the heading text as rendered: inline markup removed (`code` keeps its text, `**bold**` becomes bold, `[text](url)` becomes text, HTML tags dropped). 2. Lower-case it. 3. Remove every character that is not a letter, digit, space, hyphen or underscore (letters include accented and non-Latin letters; emoji and punctuation go). 4. Turn each space into a hyphen. Spaces are NOT collapsed: "C++ & Rust" becomes `c--rust`. 5. Duplicates get `-1`, `-2`, ... in order of appearance: the second "Usage" is `#usage-1`. | Heading | Anchor | |---|---| | `## What's new? (v2.0)` | `#whats-new-v20` | | ``## The `--dry-run` flag`` | `#the---dry-run-flag` | | `## Über uns` | `#über-uns` (GitHub also accepts the percent-encoded form) | | `## C++ & Rust: 100% safe?` | `#c--rust-100-safe` | | `## snake_case_name` | `#snake_case_name` | | `## Usage` (second time) | `#usage-1` | The script's slug function matches the github-slugger library on these cases. ## Other renderers - **GitLab**: like GitHub, but consecutive hyphens are collapsed into one (`#c-rust-100-safe`), so links copied between GitHub and GitLab can break. - **MkDocs (Python-Markdown toc)**: drops non-ASCII by default, collapses separators; `{#custom-id}` is available with attr_list. Check `markdown_extensions: toc: slugify` in mkdocs.yml. - **Docusaurus**: GitHub-like slugs; supports `## Heading {#custom-id}`. - **Hugo (goldmark)**: GitHub-like by default; `autoHeadingIDType` can be `github`, `github-ascii` or `blackfriday`. - **VS Code preview / most IDEs**: GitHub-like. If the published site and the repo view disagree, prefer explicit anchors for anything linked from outside. ## Explicit anchors - `` or `` just before the heading (works everywhere HTML is allowed). - `## Install {#install}` where the renderer supports attribute lists (MkDocs attr_list, Docusaurus, Hugo, Pandoc). On GitHub the `{#...}` shows up as literal text. ## What breaks anchors - Renaming a heading ("Configuration" -> "Configure the team folder"). - Duplicates: links to `#usage` always land on the first one. - Capital letters in the link (`#Usage`): GitHub anchors are lower-case; some browsers forgive it, many renderers do not. - Copying the anchor from another renderer (GitLab vs GitHub hyphens). - Headings generated by includes or templates the checker cannot see; mark these with `--ignore MISSING_ANCHOR` for that folder only, and say so. - Line anchors (`#L10`, `#L10-L20`) are GitHub file-view features; they are accepted but break if the file moves or lines shift. FILE:references/finding-codes.md # Finding codes | Code | Severity | Why it matters | Usual fix | |---|---|---|---| | BROKEN_LINK | HIGH | relative link to a file or folder that does not exist (moved, renamed, typo) | link to the current path; `git log --diff-filter=R --name-status -- docs/` shows renames | | BROKEN_IMAGE | HIGH | image path does not exist; readers see a broken icon | fix the path or commit the image | | MISSING_ANCHOR | HIGH | #fragment matches no heading or explicit anchor in the target file | use the suggested anchor, or add an explicit anchor | | MISSING_REF_DEF | HIGH | `[text][label]` has no `[label]: url` definition; it renders as plain bracketed text | add the definition or fix the label (labels are case-insensitive) | | DUPLICATE_ANCHOR | MEDIUM | two headings produce the same slug; the second gets `-1` and links land on the first | make headings unique, e.g. "Usage (CLI)" and "Usage (API)" | | DUPLICATE_REF_DEF | MEDIUM | the same label is defined twice; only the first counts | delete or rename one | | CASE_MISMATCH | MEDIUM | file exists only with different case; fine on macOS/Windows, broken on Linux, GitHub Pages and most CI | use the exact name | | ANCHOR_CASE | MEDIUM | anchor only matches when lower-cased | write anchors in lower case | | LOCAL_ABSOLUTE_PATH | MEDIUM | link to /Users/..., /home/..., C:\ or file:// works only on the author's machine | relative path, or remove | | EMPTY_LINK | MEDIUM | `[text]()` or empty href | fill in or remove | | EMPTY_LINK_TEXT | MEDIUM | `[](url)`: nothing to click or read aloud | add link text | | MISSING_ALT | MEDIUM | image without alt text; screen readers say "image" or the file name | describe what it shows and why it is there | | UNUSED_REF_DEF | LOW | definition never used; usually left over after an edit | delete, or link to it if the link was lost | | BARE_URL | LOW | raw URL in text; not clickable in some renderers, read character by character | `[descriptive text](url)` or `` | | OUTSIDE_ROOT | LOW | relative link leaves the docs root; breaks if docs are published alone | link to the published URL | Exit codes: 0 = no HIGH, 1 = HIGH present, 2 = bad input. Use `--min-severity` and `--ignore` to tune a CI gate, and record any ignore in the repo with a reason. ## Link forms the script understands - Inline: `[text](path.md#anchor "title")`, `[text]()`, `[text](my%20notes.md)` - Images: `![alt](img.png)`, `` - Reference: `[text][label]`, `[label][]`, `[label]` with `[label]: url "title"` anywhere in the same file - Autolinks ``, HTML ``, explicit anchors ``, ``, `{#id}` - Root-relative `/guide/a.md` resolves from `--root` (default: the first folder argument) - Skipped: fenced and indented code blocks, inline code, `mailto:`/`tel:`, GitHub line anchors, task list boxes `[ ]` `[x]` ## Checking external URLs (only when asked) - Deduplicate first: `--external` lists each URL once with every place it is used. - Use HEAD, fall back to GET when the server rejects HEAD (405) or lies about it. - One or two requests per host at a time, a 10 s timeout, a clear User-Agent. - 200-299 OK; # SQL Schema Design Reviewer

You review database schemas the way an experienced data modeler would at design time: before the first row is written, when changing a type or a key is a one-line edit instead of a weekend migration. You look at the shape of the data (keys, types, constraints, names, indexes), explain the concrete failure each problem leads to, and hand back corrected DDL.

This skill reviews the design of tables. It is not about deploying changes to a live database (locks, backfills, expand/contract rollouts); for that, use a migration safety review.

## Files in this skill

- `scripts/schema_lint.py` - parses CREATE TABLE, CREATE INDEX and ALTER TABLE ... ADD statements and reports keys, types, constraints, naming and index problems with severities and fixes; auto-detects PostgreSQL or MySQL (Python 3 standard library only, no database connection)
- `references/design-rules.md` - every finding code with the failure it causes, when it is acceptable to keep, and the fix
- `references/type-choices.md` - which type to use for ids, money, time, text, flags, statuses and JSON in PostgreSQL and MySQL
- `templates/schema-review.md` - the review to hand back
- `examples/shop-schema.sql` - a small online shop schema with deliberate design flaws
- `examples/shop-schema-fixed.sql` - the same schema after the review; it lints clean

## Workflow

### 1. Get the schema and the context
Ask for the DDL (schema.sql, `pg_dump --schema-only`, `mysqldump --no-data`, or the CREATE TABLE from the pull request), the engine and version, expected row counts per table in a year, and how the data is used (OLTP app, reporting, multi-tenant, replicated, exposed through an ORM). Ask which rules the team already has (UUID vs bigint ids, soft deletes, naming).

### 2. Run the linter
```
python3 scripts/schema_lint.py examples/shop-schema.sql
python3 scripts/schema_lint.py schema.sql --dialect mysql --min-severity MEDIUM
python3 scripts/schema_lint.py db/*.sql --ignore NO_CREATED_AT --json > schema-review.json
python3 scripts/schema_lint.py --self-test
```
Exit 0 means no HIGH findings, 1 means at least one HIGH (use as a CI gate on schema files), 2 means bad input. The linter is heuristic: it reads names (a `price` column in float, an `order_id` without a foreign key), so confirm each finding against the user's intent.

### 3. Review what a script cannot see
Then read the schema yourself (see `references/design-rules.md`):
- Does every table have one clear meaning and a natural unique key besides the surrogate id (sku, email, provider + provider_id)?
- Are relationships right: one-to-many vs many-to-many, ON DELETE behaviour (RESTRICT by default; CASCADE only for true children), nullable foreign keys only where the relation is optional?
- Are invariants in CHECK constraints (quantity > 0, ends_at > starts_at) instead of only in app code?
- Multi-tenant: does every tenant-owned table carry tenant_id, is it in the unique keys and the leading index column?
- Soft deletes: are unique constraints partial (`WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`)?
- Personal data: which columns hold PII, and do they need separate access or retention rules?

### 4. Deliver
Fill `templates/schema-review.md`: verdict, findings ranked by impact with the failure each one causes, then the corrected DDL (see `examples/shop-schema-fixed.sql`) and a list of decisions left to the team. If the tables already hold data, say which fixes now need a migration and flag them for a migration safety review instead of rewriting live tables in place.

## Example result
`examples/shop-schema.sql` (PostgreSQL, 5 tables): 20 findings, 4 HIGH. order_items has no primary key (duplicate lines possible); products.price is double precision and payments.amount is real (cents drift); payments.order_id is integer but references "order".id (bigserial). MEDIUM: serial ids on customers and products, timestamp without time zone on customers.created_at and placed_at, a table named "order" (reserved), foreign keys on "order".customer_id and order_items.order_id with no index. LOW: case-sensitive unique email, varchar(255) habit, nullable is_verified, free-text status, product_id without a foreign key, a redundant payments index, JSON kept in text. `examples/shop-schema-fixed.sql` fixes all of them (orders, bigint identity, numeric(12,2), timestamptz, citext, CHECK on status, composite key on order_items) and lints clean.

## Rules

- Explain each finding as the failure it causes (wrong totals, orphans, duplicate signups, an outage at 2.1 billion ids), not as a style rule.
- Keep the user's conventions (UUID ids, naming) unless they cause a real problem; say when a finding is a judgement call.
- Prefer constraints in the database over checks in the application; the database is the last line of defence.
- Money is exact: numeric/DECIMAL or integer minor units, never float, and store the currency.
- Time is an instant: timestamptz in PostgreSQL, UTC everywhere in MySQL.
- Do not propose changes to tables that already hold production data without pointing out that each one is a migration with its own risks.

# Design rules and finding codes

| Code | Sev | What goes wrong | Acceptable when | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NO_PRIMARY_KEY | HIGH | duplicate rows cannot be told apart or deleted one at a time; logical replication and CDC need a key; ORMs misbehave | never for OLTP tables (staging tables loaded and dropped in one job, maybe) | surrogate `id bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY` or a composite natural key (order_id, product_id) |
| FLOAT_MONEY | HIGH | 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.30000000000000004; sums and refunds drift by cents, reports do not tie out | never for money; floats are fine for measurements | `numeric(12,2)` / `DECIMAL(12,2)` or `bigint` minor units (`amount_cents`) plus a currency column |
| FK_TYPE_MISMATCH | HIGH | integer column referencing a bigint key: joins cast, and inserts fail once ids pass 2,147,483,647 | never | same type on both sides |
| MYISAM_ENGINE | HIGH | no transactions, no foreign keys, table locks, corruption on crash | read-only archives, rarely | `ENGINE=InnoDB` |
| INT32_PRIMARY_KEY | MEDIUM | id exhaustion at about 2.1 billion (sequences also skip on rollbacks); the fix is a full table rewrite on the biggest table | small lookup tables (statuses, countries) | `bigint` identity / `BIGINT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT` |
| TIMESTAMP_WITHOUT_TZ | MEDIUM | the stored value means different instants depending on the writer's zone; DST and server moves corrupt ordering | local wall-clock values that are not instants (store opening hours, a birthday time) | `timestamptz` |
| MONEY_TYPE | MEDIUM | Postgres `money` follows lc_monetary, one currency, rounding on division | never in new schemas | `numeric(12,2)` + currency |
| NULLABLE_AUDIT_COLUMN | MEDIUM | rows without created_at break "last 7 days" reports and backfills | never | `NOT NULL DEFAULT now()` |
| FK_WITHOUT_INDEX | MEDIUM | (PostgreSQL) deleting or updating a parent scans the whole child table under lock; joins from parent to children are slow. MySQL InnoDB creates the index itself | tiny child tables, parents never deleted | index whose leading columns are the FK columns |
| RESERVED_WORD_NAME | MEDIUM | `order`, `user`, `group` must be quoted in every query, ORM, BI tool and ad-hoc psql session | never in new schemas | plural or qualified names: orders, app_users, user_groups, sort_order |
| MYSQL_UTF8MB3 | MEDIUM | `utf8` is 3-byte: emoji and some CJK characters fail or are cut | never in new schemas | `utf8mb4` + `utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci` |
| NULLABLE_BOOLEAN | LOW | three-valued logic: `WHERE NOT is_verified` skips NULL rows | when "unknown" is a real state (then prefer an explicit status) | `NOT NULL DEFAULT false` |
| UNCHECKED_STATUS | LOW | 'Shipped', 'shipped ', 'shiped' all appear; reports split | statuses owned by another system you only mirror | `CHECK (status IN (...))`, an enum type or a lookup table FK |
| MISSING_FOREIGN_KEY | LOW | orphans after deletes, typos in ids, no documented relation | cross-database or event-sourced references; document them | `REFERENCES parent(id)` + index |
| CASE_SENSITIVE_UNIQUE_EMAIL | LOW | Ana@x.com and ana@x.com are two accounts; password resets go to the wrong one | never for login emails | `citext` or `UNIQUE INDEX ON t (lower(email))` and normalize on write |
| VARCHAR_255_HABIT | LOW | in Postgres, 255 is an arbitrary MySQL-era limit; real rules are missing and odd values get rejected | when 255 really is the rule | `text` + `CHECK (char_length(x) <= n)` for real limits |
| REDUNDANT_INDEX | LOW | an index that is a prefix of another (or of the PK) costs writes and memory for nothing | the shorter index is much smaller and very hot | drop it |
| JSON_IN_TEXT | LOW | no validation, no operators, no GIN index | the text is not really JSON | `jsonb` / `JSON` |
| NO_CREATED_AT | LOW | debugging, audits and backfills need to know when rows appeared | pure join tables | `created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()` |
| MIXED_CASE_NAME | LOW | quoted "OrderItems" must be quoted forever in Postgres | never | snake_case |
| DATETIME_NO_ZONE | LOW | (MySQL) DATETIME has no zone; mixed writers store mixed zones | when every connection sets time_zone='+00:00' | enforce UTC |

## Things the linter cannot judge (review by hand)
- **Keys**: is there a natural unique key besides the surrogate id? Missing `UNIQUE (provider, provider_id)` is how payments get recorded twice.
- **ON DELETE**: RESTRICT/NO ACTION by default; CASCADE only for true child rows (order_items of an order), never from customers to payments.
- **CHECK constraints for invariants**: `quantity > 0`, `ends_at > starts_at`, `discount <= total`.
- **Multi-tenancy**: tenant_id on every tenant table, first in unique keys and indexes, and in every FK (composite FKs prevent cross-tenant references).
- **Soft deletes**: partial unique indexes `WHERE deleted_at IS NULL`, or the email can never be reused.
- **Denormalized totals**: if orders.total is stored, say how it stays equal to the sum of order_items.
- **PII**: list columns with personal data; consider a separate table with stricter access and retention.

# Type choices (PostgreSQL / MySQL 8)

| Data | PostgreSQL | MySQL 8 | Avoid |
|---|---|---|---|
| Surrogate id | `bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY` | `BIGINT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT` | `serial`/`int` on growing tables |
| Public / distributed id | `uuid` (UUIDv7 for index locality, `gen_random_uuid()` for v4) | `BINARY(16)` with UUID_TO_BIN(x, 1) | `varchar(36)` UUIDs (3x bigger, slower) |
| Money | `numeric(12,2)` (or (19,4) for rates) + `currency char(3)` | `DECIMAL(12,2)` + `CHAR(3)` | `float`, `double`, `real`, Postgres `money` |
| Money as integer | `bigint amount_cents` (mind currencies with 0 or 3 decimals) | `BIGINT` | `int` cents (overflows at 21 million) |
| Instant (event happened) | `timestamptz` | `DATETIME(6)` in UTC, or `TIMESTAMP` (2038 limit, converted by session zone) | `timestamp` without time zone |
| Calendar date | `date` | `DATE` | timestamps at midnight |
| Wall-clock time / schedule | `time` + an IANA zone column | `TIME` + zone column | `timetz` |
| Duration | `interval` or integer seconds | `INT` seconds | text like "1h30" |
| Text | `text` (+ CHECK for real limits) | `VARCHAR(n)` with a real n; `TEXT` for long bodies | `varchar(255)` by habit; `char(n)` padding |
| Case-insensitive text (email, username) | `citext` or a `lower()` unique index | case-insensitive `_ci` collation (default) | plain unique on text in Postgres |
| Flag | `boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false` | `BOOLEAN` (TINYINT(1)) `NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` | nullable booleans, 'Y'/'N' strings |
| Status | `text` + `CHECK (... IN (...))`, enum type, or lookup table | `ENUM(...)` or lookup table | unconstrained text |
| JSON | `jsonb` (GIN index for containment) | `JSON` (generated columns to index) | JSON in text |
| IP address | `inet` / `cidr` | `VARBINARY(16)` with INET6_ATON | text |
| Large binary | object storage + key in a `text` column | same | big BLOBs in hot tables |

## Notes
- Changing a column type later rewrites the table in both engines (with a few exceptions such as widening varchar in Postgres). Get ids and money right first.
- Enum types in Postgres: adding a value is cheap, removing or renaming one is not. Lookup tables are easier to evolve and can carry labels and sort order.
- `NOT NULL` with a sensible default is the norm; nullable should mean "genuinely unknown or not applicable".
- Store the currency next to every amount, even if today there is only one.
- Name things the same everywhere: `customer_id` in every table that references customers, `_at` for instants, `_on` or `_date` for dates, `is_`/`has_` for booleans.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""SQL schema design linter for PostgreSQL and MySQL DDL (Python 3 standard library only).

Reads CREATE TABLE / CREATE INDEX / ALTER TABLE ... ADD statements (a schema dump,
schema.sql, or the DDL of new tables in a pull request) and reports design problems
that are cheap to fix before data exists and expensive after: tables without a
primary key, money stored in floating point, foreign keys whose type differs from the
referenced key or that have no supporting index (PostgreSQL), *_id columns without a
foreign key, 32-bit primary keys, timestamps without time zone, nullable audit
columns and booleans, unchecked status columns, reserved-word and mixed-case names,
case-sensitive unique emails, redundant indexes, JSON kept in text columns, and MySQL
tables using MyISAM or 3-byte utf8.

It does not connect to a database and does not judge migration safety (locks,
backfills); it reviews the shape of the schema itself.

Usage:
  python3 schema_lint.py FILE.sql [FILE.sql ...] [--dialect auto|postgres|mysql]
        [--min-severity LOW|MEDIUM|HIGH] [--ignore CODE,CODE] [--json]
  python3 schema_lint.py --self-test
Exit codes: 0 = no HIGH findings, 1 = HIGH findings, 2 = bad input (unreadable file,
no CREATE TABLE found).
"""
import argparse, json, re, sys

SEV_ORDER = {"HIGH": 0, "MEDIUM": 1, "LOW": 2}
MONEY_RE = re.compile(r"(^|_)(price|amount|total|subtotal|cost|balance|fee|fees|tax|salary|refund|discount|paid|payment|revenue|credit|debit|charge)(_|$)", re.I)
RESERVED = {"user", "order", "group", "select", "table", "column", "desc", "asc", "check", "default", "from",
            "where", "limit", "offset", "references", "primary", "key", "range", "rank", "window", "all", "both",
            "end", "grant", "to", "type", "values", "constraint", "index", "match", "condition", "interval", "read", "row"}
RESERVED_PG_ONLY_SAFE = {"key", "range", "rank", "type", "values", "match", "condition", "interval", "read", "row", "index"}  # fine unquoted in Postgres
RESERVED_MY_ONLY_SAFE = {"offset", "user", "end", "type", "values", "row"}  # fine unquoted in MySQL 8
STATUS_RE = re.compile(r"^(status|state|kind|role|type|.*_status|.*_state|.*_type)$", re.I)
JSONISH_RE = re.compile(r"(^|_)(json|payload|metadata|meta|attributes|settings|extra|data)$", re.I)
INT32 = {"int", "integer", "int4", "serial", "serial4", "mediumint", "smallint", "int2", "smallserial", "tinyint"}
INT64 = {"bigint", "int8", "bigserial", "serial8"}


def finding(sev, code, table, column, problem, fix, line=0):
    return {"severity": sev, "code": code, "table": table, "column": column, "line": line, "problem": problem, "fix": fix}


def strip_comments(sql):
    out, i, n = [], 0, len(sql)
    while i < n:
        c = sql[i]
        if c in "'\"`":
            j = i + 1
            while j < n and sql[j] != c:
                j += 2 if sql[j] == "\\" and c == "'" else 1
            out.append(sql[i:j + 1]); i = j + 1
        elif sql.startswith("--", i) or c == "#" and (i == 0 or sql[i - 1] in "\n \t"):
            j = sql.find("\n", i); j = n if j < 0 else j
            out.append(" " * (j - i)); i = j
        elif sql.startswith("/*", i):
            j = sql.find("*/", i + 2); j = n if j < 0 else j + 2
            out.append(re.sub(r"[^\n]", " ", sql[i:j])); i = j
        else:
            out.append(c); i += 1
    return "".join(out)


def split_top(s, sep=","):
    parts, depth, cur, q = [], 0, [], None
    for ch in s:
        if q:
            cur.append(ch)
            if ch == q:
                q = None
            continue
        if ch in "'\"`":
            q = ch
        elif ch == "(":
            depth += 1
        elif ch == ")":
            depth -= 1
        if ch == sep and depth == 0:
            parts.append("".join(cur)); cur = []
        else:
            cur.append(ch)
    if "".join(cur).strip():
        parts.append("".join(cur))
    return parts


def statements(sql):
    clean = strip_comments(sql)
    pos = 0
    for part in split_top(clean, ";"):
        line = clean.count("\n", 0, pos + len(part) - len(part.lstrip())) + 1
        pos += len(part) + 1
        if part.strip():
            yield line, part.strip()


def ident(s):
    s = s.strip()
    quoted = s[:1] in "\"`"
    name = s.split(".")[-1].strip().strip("\"`")
    return name, quoted


def cols_list(s):
    return [ident(re.sub(r"\s+(ASC|DESC|NULLS\s+(FIRST|LAST)).*$", "", c.strip(), flags=re.I))[0].lower() if not c.strip().startswith("(") and "(" not in c else c.strip().lower()
            for c in split_top(s)]


class Schema:
    def __init__(self):
        self.tables, self.indexes, self.fks, self.enums = {}, [], [], set()
        self.dialect_hints = {"mysql": 0, "postgres": 0}


def parse(sql):
    sc = Schema()
    if re.search(r"AUTO_INCREMENT|ENGINE\s*=|`|UNSIGNED|DATETIME|TINYINT\(", sql, re.I):
        sc.dialect_hints["mysql"] += 1
    if re.search(r"\bSERIAL\b|BIGSERIAL|TIMESTAMPTZ|JSONB|GENERATED\s+(ALWAYS|BY DEFAULT)\s+AS\s+IDENTITY|::|CREATE\s+TYPE|CITEXT|CONCURRENTLY|\bTEXT\[\]", sql, re.I):
        sc.dialect_hints["postgres"] += 1
    for line, st in statements(sql):
        m = re.match(r"CREATE\s+(?:TEMP(?:ORARY)?\s+|UNLOGGED\s+)?TABLE\s+(?:IF\s+NOT\s+EXISTS\s+)?([\w\".`]+)\s*\((.*)\)\s*(.*)$", st, re.I | re.S)
        if m:
            name, quoted = ident(m.group(1))
            t = {"name": name, "quoted": quoted, "line": line, "cols": {}, "order": [], "pk": [], "uniques": [],
                 "checks": " ".join([]), "options": m.group(3), "raw": st}
            checks = []
            for item in split_top(m.group(2)):
                parse_item(item.strip(), t, sc, checks)
            t["checks"] = " ".join(checks).lower()
            sc.tables[name.lower()] = t
            continue
        m = re.match(r"CREATE\s+(UNIQUE\s+)?INDEX\s+(?:CONCURRENTLY\s+)?(?:IF\s+NOT\s+EXISTS\s+)?([\w\".`]*)\s*ON\s+(?:ONLY\s+)?([\w\".`]+)\s*(?:USING\s+\w+\s*)?\((.*)\)\s*(.*)$", st, re.I | re.S)
        if m:
            sc.indexes.append({"table": ident(m.group(3))[0].lower(), "cols": cols_list(m.group(4)), "unique": bool(m.group(1)),
                               "name": ident(m.group(2))[0] if m.group(2) else "", "partial": "where" in m.group(5).lower(), "line": line})
            continue
        m = re.match(r"ALTER\s+TABLE\s+(?:ONLY\s+)?(?:IF\s+EXISTS\s+)?([\w\".`]+)\s+(.*)$", st, re.I | re.S)
        if m:
            tname = ident(m.group(1))[0].lower()
            for action in split_top(m.group(2)):
                a = action.strip()
                am = re.match(r"ADD\s+(?:COLUMN\s+)(?:IF\s+NOT\s+EXISTS\s+)?(.*)$", a, re.I | re.S)
                if am and tname in sc.tables:
                    parse_item(am.group(1), sc.tables[tname], sc, [])
                    continue
                am = re.match(r"ADD\s+(.*)$", a, re.I | re.S)
                if am and tname in sc.tables:
                    chk = []
                    parse_item(am.group(1), sc.tables[tname], sc, chk)
                    sc.tables[tname]["checks"] += " " + " ".join(chk).lower()
            continue
        m = re.match(r"CREATE\s+TYPE\s+([\w\".]+)\s+AS\s+ENUM", st, re.I)
        if m:
            sc.enums.add(ident(m.group(1))[0].lower())
        m = re.match(r"CREATE\s+(?:DOMAIN|EXTENSION)\s+(?:IF\s+NOT\s+EXISTS\s+)?([\w\".]+)", st, re.I)
        if m:
            sc.enums.add(ident(m.group(1))[0].lower())
    return sc


def parse_item(item, t, sc, checks):
    u = item.upper()
    m = re.match(r"CONSTRAINT\s+[\w\"`]+\s+(.*)$", item, re.I | re.S)
    if m:
        item, u = m.group(1).strip(), m.group(1).strip().upper()
    if u.startswith("PRIMARY KEY"):
        t["pk"] = cols_list(re.search(r"\((.*)\)", item, re.S).group(1)); return
    if re.match(r"UNIQUE\b", u):
        cm = re.search(r"\((.*?)\)", item, re.S)
        if cm:
            cols = cols_list(cm.group(1))
            t["uniques"].append(cols)
            sc.indexes.append({"table": t["name"].lower(), "cols": cols, "unique": True, "name": "", "partial": False, "line": t["line"]})
        return
    if u.startswith("FOREIGN KEY"):
        fm = re.match(r"FOREIGN\s+KEY\s*\((.*?)\)\s*REFERENCES\s+([\w\".`]+)\s*(?:\((.*?)\))?", item, re.I | re.S)
        if fm:
            sc.fks.append({"table": t["name"].lower(), "cols": cols_list(fm.group(1)), "ref": ident(fm.group(2))[0].lower(),
                           "ref_cols": cols_list(fm.group(3)) if fm.group(3) else None})
        return
    if u.startswith("CHECK"):
        checks.append(item); return
    if re.match(r"(UNIQUE\s+)?(KEY|INDEX)\b", u) or re.match(r"(FULLTEXT|SPATIAL)\b", u):
        cm = re.search(r"\((.*)\)", item, re.S)
        if cm:
            sc.indexes.append({"table": t["name"].lower(), "cols": cols_list(cm.group(1)), "unique": u.startswith("UNIQUE"),
                               "name": "", "partial": False, "line": t["line"]})
        return
    if u.startswith(("EXCLUDE", "LIKE", "PERIOD")):
        return
    cm = re.match(r"([\"`][^\"`]+[\"`]|[\w$]+)\s+(.*)$", item, re.S)
    if not cm:
        return
    name, quoted = ident(cm.group(1))
    rest = cm.group(2)
    tm = re.match(r"((?:double\s+precision|character\s+varying|bit\s+varying|timestamp(?:\s*\(\d+\))?(?:\s+with(?:out)?\s+time\s+zone)?(?!\w)|time(?:\s+with(?:out)?\s+time\s+zone)?(?!\w)|[\w.]+)(?:\s*\([^)]*\))?(?:\s+unsigned)?(?:\s*\[\])?)", rest, re.I)
    ctype = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", tm.group(1).lower()) if tm else ""
    ru = rest.upper()
    col = {"name": name, "quoted": quoted, "type": ctype, "not_null": "NOT NULL" in ru or "PRIMARY KEY" in ru,
           "default": "DEFAULT" in ru or "IDENTITY" in ru or "AUTO_INCREMENT" in ru or ctype.endswith("serial"),
           "check": "CHECK" in ru}
    t["cols"][name.lower()] = col
    t["order"].append(name.lower())
    if "PRIMARY KEY" in ru:
        t["pk"] = [name.lower()]
    if re.search(r"\bUNIQUE\b", ru):
        t["uniques"].append([name.lower()])
        sc.indexes.append({"table": t["name"].lower(), "cols": [name.lower()], "unique": True, "name": "", "partial": False, "line": t["line"]})
    rm = re.search(r"REFERENCES\s+([\w\".`]+)\s*(?:\((.*?)\))?", rest, re.I)
    if rm:
        sc.fks.append({"table": t["name"].lower(), "cols": [name.lower()], "ref": ident(rm.group(1))[0].lower(),
                       "ref_cols": cols_list(rm.group(2)) if rm.group(2) else None})
    if col["check"]:
        checks.append(f"check ({name})")


def qi(name):
    return f'"{name}"' if name.lower() in RESERVED or name != name.lower() else name


def base_type(ctype):
    t = re.sub(r"\(.*?\)|\s+unsigned|\[\]", "", ctype).strip()
    return {"int4": "integer", "int": "integer", "serial": "integer", "serial4": "integer", "int8": "bigint",
            "bigserial": "bigint", "serial8": "bigint", "int2": "smallint", "smallserial": "smallint"}.get(t, t)


def lint(sql, dialect="auto", ignore=()):
    sc = parse(sql)
    if dialect == "auto":
        dialect = "mysql" if sc.dialect_hints["mysql"] > sc.dialect_hints["postgres"] else "postgres"
    out = []

    def add(*a, **k):
        f = finding(*a, **k)
        if f["code"] not in ignore:
            out.append(f)

    table_names = set(sc.tables)
    for key, t in sc.tables.items():
        tn = t["name"]
        ln = t["line"]
        if not t["pk"]:
            add("HIGH", "NO_PRIMARY_KEY", tn, "", "table has no primary key: duplicate rows cannot be told apart, updates and replication (logical replication, MySQL row-based, CDC) suffer",
                "add a bigint identity (or UUID) primary key, or a composite key on the natural unique columns", line=ln)
        elif len(t["pk"]) == 1 and t["pk"][0] in t["cols"]:
            c = t["cols"][t["pk"][0]]
            bt = base_type(c["type"])
            if bt in {"integer", "smallint", "mediumint", "tinyint"} and not re.search(r"(^|_)(type|status|kind|country|currency|lookup)s?$", tn, re.I):
                add("MEDIUM", "INT32_PRIMARY_KEY", tn, c["name"], f"primary key {c['name']} is {c['type']} (max about 2.1 billion, less for smaller types); running out means an emergency type change on the biggest table",
                    "use bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY (Postgres) or BIGINT UNSIGNED AUTO_INCREMENT (MySQL)", line=ln)
        if dialect == "postgres" and t["quoted"] and t["name"] != t["name"].lower():
            add("LOW", "MIXED_CASE_NAME", tn, "", f'table "{tn}" is quoted mixed case: every query must quote it forever', "use snake_case lower-case names", line=ln)
        if tn.lower() in RESERVED and not (dialect == "postgres" and tn.lower() in RESERVED_PG_ONLY_SAFE) and not (dialect == "mysql" and tn.lower() in RESERVED_MY_ONLY_SAFE):
            add("MEDIUM", "RESERVED_WORD_NAME", tn, "", f"table name '{tn}' is a reserved word and must be quoted in every query and ORM", "rename (e.g. users, orders, user_groups)", line=ln)
        if dialect == "mysql":
            opts = t["options"].lower()
            if re.search(r"engine\s*=\s*myisam", opts):
                add("HIGH", "MYISAM_ENGINE", tn, "", "ENGINE=MyISAM has no transactions, no foreign keys and table-level locks; crashes can corrupt it", "use ENGINE=InnoDB", line=ln)
            if re.search(r"charset\s*=\s*utf8(mb3)?\b(?!mb4)", opts):
                add("MEDIUM", "MYSQL_UTF8MB3", tn, "", "utf8 in MySQL is 3-byte utf8mb3: emoji and some CJK characters fail to insert or get mangled", "use DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci", line=ln)
        if not any(re.match(r"^(created_at|created|created_on|inserted_at|date_created|creation_date)$", c) for c in t["cols"]):
            add("LOW", "NO_CREATED_AT", tn, "", "no created_at column: hard to debug, audit or backfill later", "add created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()", line=ln)
        v255 = [c["name"] for c in t["cols"].values() if re.match(r"(varchar|character varying)\s*\(255\)", c["type"])]
        if dialect == "postgres" and len(v255) >= 3:
            add("LOW", "VARCHAR_255_HABIT", tn, ", ".join(v255), f"{len(v255)} columns are varchar(255): in Postgres the limit costs nothing to drop but 255 is rarely the real rule",
                "use text, with a CHECK (char_length(x) <= n) where a real limit exists", line=ln)
        for cname in t["order"]:
            c = t["cols"][cname]
            ct, bt = c["type"], base_type(c["type"])
            cn = c["name"]
            if MONEY_RE.search(cn) and bt in {"float", "real", "double", "double precision", "float4", "float8"}:
                add("HIGH", "FLOAT_MONEY", tn, cn, f"{cn} is {ct}: binary floating point cannot store 0.10 exactly, sums drift by cents",
                    "use numeric(12,2) / DECIMAL(12,2), or bigint minor units (amount_cents)", line=ln)
            if bt == "money" and dialect == "postgres":
                add("MEDIUM", "MONEY_TYPE", tn, cn, "Postgres money type depends on lc_monetary, has one fixed currency and rounds", "use numeric(12,2) plus a currency column", line=ln)
            if dialect == "postgres" and (re.match(r"^timestamp(\s*\(\d+\))?$", ct) or "without time zone" in ct):
                add("MEDIUM", "TIMESTAMP_WITHOUT_TZ", tn, cn, f"{cn} is timestamp without time zone: the instant depends on whatever zone the writer assumed", "use timestamptz (stores an absolute instant, displays in the session zone)", line=ln)
            if dialect == "mysql" and bt == "datetime" and re.search(r"_at$", cn):
                add("LOW", "DATETIME_NO_ZONE", tn, cn, f"{cn} is DATETIME (no zone): make sure every writer stores UTC", "document and enforce UTC (time_zone='+00:00' on connections) or use TIMESTAMP within its 2038 range", line=ln)
            if re.match(r"^(created_at|updated_at|inserted_at)$", cn, re.I) and not c["not_null"]:
                add("MEDIUM", "NULLABLE_AUDIT_COLUMN", tn, cn, f"{cn} is nullable{'' if c['default'] else ' and has no default'}: rows without it will appear", f"{cn} timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()", line=ln)
            if bt in {"boolean", "bool"} and not c["not_null"]:
                add("LOW", "NULLABLE_BOOLEAN", tn, cn, f"{cn} is a nullable boolean: three states (true, false, unknown) and NULL-unsafe WHERE clauses", f"{cn} boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false", line=ln)
            if STATUS_RE.match(cn) and re.match(r"^(text|varchar|character varying|char|character)", bt) and not c["check"] \
                    and cn.lower() not in t["checks"] and not any(f["table"] == key and cname in f["cols"] for f in sc.fks):
                add("LOW", "UNCHECKED_STATUS", tn, cn, f"{cn} is free text: typos like 'Shipped ' and 'shiped' will end up in the data", "add CHECK (status IN (...)), an enum type, or a FK to a lookup table", line=ln)
            if bt in {"text", "longtext", "mediumtext"} and JSONISH_RE.search(cn):
                add("LOW", "JSON_IN_TEXT", tn, cn, f"{cn} looks like JSON stored as {ct}: no validation, no indexing", "use jsonb (Postgres) or JSON (MySQL) if it really is JSON", line=ln)
            if cn.lower() in RESERVED and not (dialect == "postgres" and cn.lower() in RESERVED_PG_ONLY_SAFE) and not (dialect == "mysql" and cn.lower() in RESERVED_MY_ONLY_SAFE) and cn.lower() not in {"type"}:
                add("MEDIUM", "RESERVED_WORD_NAME", tn, cn, f"column name '{cn}' is a reserved word and needs quoting everywhere", "rename it (e.g. sort_order, user_id, group_name, ends_at)", line=ln)
            if dialect == "postgres" and c["quoted"] and cn != cn.lower():
                add("LOW", "MIXED_CASE_NAME", tn, cn, f'column "{cn}" is quoted mixed case: every query must quote it', "use snake_case", line=ln)
            if cn.lower().endswith("_id") and cname not in t["pk"] and not any(f["table"] == key and cname in f["cols"] for f in sc.fks):
                stem = cn.lower()[:-3]
                cands = [x for x in (stem, stem + "s", stem + "es", stem[:-1] + "ies" if stem.endswith("y") else None) if x and x in table_names]
                if cands:
                    add("LOW", "MISSING_FOREIGN_KEY", tn, cn, f"{cn} looks like a reference to {cands[0]} but has no foreign key: orphans and typos are possible", f"add REFERENCES {cands[0]}(id) (with an index)", line=ln)
            if re.search(r"(^|_)email$", cn, re.I) and [cname] in t["uniques"] and dialect == "postgres" and bt != "citext":
                if not any(i["table"] == key and any("lower(" in c2 for c2 in i["cols"]) for i in sc.indexes):
                    add("LOW", "CASE_SENSITIVE_UNIQUE_EMAIL", tn, cn, "UNIQUE on email is case-sensitive in Postgres: Ana@x.com and ana@x.com can both sign up", "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... ON t (lower(email)) or use citext", line=ln)
    # foreign keys: types and indexes
    for f in sc.fks:
        t = sc.tables.get(f["table"])
        r = sc.tables.get(f["ref"])
        if not t:
            continue
        ref_cols = f["ref_cols"] or (r["pk"] if r else None)
        if r and ref_cols and len(ref_cols) == len(f["cols"]):
            for c, rc in zip(f["cols"], ref_cols):
                a, b = t["cols"].get(c), r["cols"].get(rc)
                if a and b and base_type(a["type"]) != base_type(b["type"]) and not ({base_type(a["type"]), base_type(b["type"])} <= {"uuid"}):
                    add("HIGH", "FK_TYPE_MISMATCH", t["name"], a["name"], f"{a['name']} is {a['type']} but references {r['name']}.{b['name']} ({b['type']}): joins need casts and the FK fails once ids pass the smaller range",
                        f"make {a['name']} the same type as {r['name']}.{b['name']}", line=t["line"])
        if dialect == "postgres":
            covered = any(idx["table"] == f["table"] and not idx["partial"] and idx["cols"][:len(f["cols"])] == f["cols"] for idx in sc.indexes) \
                or t["pk"][:len(f["cols"])] == f["cols"] or any(u[:len(f["cols"])] == f["cols"] for u in t["uniques"])
            if not covered:
                add("MEDIUM", "FK_WITHOUT_INDEX", t["name"], ", ".join(f["cols"]), f"foreign key ({', '.join(f['cols'])}) -> {f['ref']} has no index starting with it: deletes/updates on {f['ref']} scan {t['name']}, and joins are slow",
                    f"CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY ON {qi(t['name'])} ({', '.join(f['cols'])})", line=t["line"])
    # redundant indexes
    for i, a in enumerate(sc.indexes):
        t = sc.tables.get(a["table"])
        if not t or a["partial"] or any("(" in c for c in a["cols"]):
            continue
        others = [b for j, b in enumerate(sc.indexes) if j != i and b["table"] == a["table"] and not b["partial"]]
        if t["pk"] and a["cols"] == t["pk"][:len(a["cols"])] and not a["unique"]:
            add("LOW", "REDUNDANT_INDEX", t["name"], ", ".join(a["cols"]), f"index on ({', '.join(a['cols'])}) duplicates the primary key's leading columns", "drop it", line=a["line"])
            continue
        for b in others:
            if len(b["cols"]) > len(a["cols"]) and b["cols"][:len(a["cols"])] == a["cols"] and not a["unique"]:
                add("LOW", "REDUNDANT_INDEX", t["name"], ", ".join(a["cols"]), f"index on ({', '.join(a['cols'])}) is a prefix of the index on ({', '.join(b['cols'])})", "drop the shorter one unless it is much smaller and hot", line=a["line"])
                break
            if b["cols"] == a["cols"] and j_before(sc.indexes, b, a) and a["unique"] == b["unique"]:
                add("LOW", "REDUNDANT_INDEX", t["name"], ", ".join(a["cols"]), f"two indexes on ({', '.join(a['cols'])})", "drop one", line=a["line"])
                break
    out.sort(key=lambda f: (SEV_ORDER[f["severity"]], f["table"], f["column"], f["code"]))
    return dialect, sc, out


def j_before(lst, b, a):
    return lst.index(b) < lst.index(a)


def report(path, dialect, sc, found):
    counts = {s: sum(1 for f in found if f["severity"] == s) for s in SEV_ORDER}
    out = [f"# Schema review: {path} ({dialect})", "",
           f"Tables: {len(sc.tables)}   Indexes: {len(sc.indexes)}   Foreign keys: {len(sc.fks)}   Findings: {len(found)} (HIGH {counts['HIGH']}, MEDIUM {counts['MEDIUM']}, LOW {counts['LOW']})", ""]
    if not found:
        out.append("No findings.")
        return "\n".join(out)
    out += ["| Sev | Code | Table.Column | Problem | Fix |", "|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    for f in found:
        loc = f["table"] + ("." + f["column"] if f["column"] else "")
        out.append(f"| {f['severity']} | {f['code']} | {loc} | {f['problem'].replace('|', '/')} | {f['fix'].replace('|', '/')} |")
    return "\n".join(out)

    print(("PASS " if ok else "FAIL ") + "empty report")

def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="SQL schema design linter (Postgres/MySQL DDL)")
    ap.add_argument("files", nargs="*")
    ap.add_argument("--dialect", default="auto", choices=["auto", "postgres", "mysql"])
    ap.add_argument("--min-severity", default="LOW", choices=list(SEV_ORDER))
    ap.add_argument("--ignore", default="")
    ap.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--self-test", action="store_true")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    if a.self_test:
        return self_test()
    if not a.files:
        ap.print_usage(sys.stderr)
        return 2
    ignore = {c.strip() for c in a.ignore.split(",") if c.strip()}
    sql_all = []
    for p in a.files:
        try:
            with open(p, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                sql_all.append(fh.read())
        except OSError as e:
            print(f"error: cannot read {p}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
    dialect, sc, found = lint("\n;\n".join(sql_all), a.dialect, ignore)
    if not sc.tables:
        print("error: no CREATE TABLE statements found", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    found = [f for f in found if SEV_ORDER[f["severity"]] <= SEV_ORDER[a.min_severity]]
    if a.json:
        print(json.dumps({"dialect": dialect, "tables": len(sc.tables), "findings": found}, indent=2))
    else:
        print(report(", ".join(a.files), dialect, sc, found))
    return 1 if any(f["severity"] == "HIGH" for f in found) else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Time Zone Meeting Slot Finder

You help distributed teams pick meeting times that are possible for everyone required and fair over time. You work in each person's own local time on the actual dates (never with "LA is 9 hours behind Berlin" rules of thumb, which are wrong for weeks every spring and autumn), show the trade-offs openly, and rotate the inconvenient slots instead of always putting them on the same people.

## Files in this skill

- `scripts/slot_finder.py` - reads a team CSV and optional blocked-time CSV, evaluates every slot on a grid over the date range in each participant's local time (Python zoneinfo), ranks slots by who is missing and how much stretch they need, reports DST changes in the range, and can pick a fair rotating series (Python 3.9+ standard library only)
- `references/dst-and-time-zone-pitfalls.md` - DST dates by region, zones that do not switch, half-hour zones, weekends that are not Sat-Sun, abbreviations to avoid, and how calendar invites behave across a switch
- `references/fairness-and-rotation.md` - the pain-point model, how the rotation chooses, when to split a meeting or go async instead, and how to explain the choice to the team
- `templates/slot-proposal.md` - the proposal to send to the team
- `examples/team.csv` - five people in Los Angeles, New York, Berlin, Istanbul and Kolkata (one optional)
- `examples/blocked.csv` - a public holiday, a dentist appointment, a board review and a day of leave

## Workflow

### 1. Collect the facts
For each participant: name, IANA zone (city based, e.g. `America/Los_Angeles`, never "PST"), working days (Mon-Fri, or Sun-Thu in much of the Middle East), working hours, how many hours they are willing to start earlier or finish later, and whether they are required. Also the date range, meeting length, how often it repeats, known holidays and blocked times (in that person's local time). Ask rather than guess zones from a city that has several (e.g. a "Mexico" team member).

### 2. Run the finder
```
python3 scripts/slot_finder.py --team examples/team.csv --blocked examples/blocked.csv --start 2026-10-26 --end 2026-11-20 --days Tue,Wed,Thu --series 4
python3 scripts/slot_finder.py --team team.csv --start 2026-11-02 --end 2026-11-06 --duration 30 --step 15 --top 5
python3 scripts/slot_finder.py --team team.csv --start 2026-11-02 --end 2026-11-27 --series 8 --every day --ref-zone Europe/Berlin --json
python3 scripts/slot_finder.py --self-test
```
Dates (`--start`, `--end`, `--days`) are read in `--ref-zone` (default UTC). Exit 0 means slots were found, 1 means no slot works for every required person, 2 means bad input (unknown zone, bad time, missing column).

### 3. Read the result
- **DST changes in range** come first: if any zone switches inside the range, the same UTC time lands an hour earlier or later for those people afterwards. Propose slots per period, not one UTC time for the whole range.
- **Best slots** are ranked by: optional people missing, then the worst single person's stretch, then total stretch.
- **Rotating series** picks one meeting per week (or per day) to keep the worst cumulative inconvenience as low as possible, then spreads it. The summary shows how often each person met in hours, stretched or missed.
- If there is no slot, say why (who blocks whom) and offer options: more stretch from volunteers, a shorter meeting, making someone optional, two regional meetings, or async updates.

### 4. Deliver
Fill `templates/slot-proposal.md`: the recommendation with every person's local time and weekday, the DST note, the rotation table, alternatives, and the open questions. Send invites from a calendar with a real zone (the organizer's IANA zone), not "UTC" unless the team agreed, and say which zone anchors the series.

## Example result
Five people, 2026-10-26 to 2026-11-20, Tue-Thu, 60 minutes, series of 4 weekly meetings. Europe left summer time on 25 October and the US on 1 November, so in the week of 26 October New York is only 5 hours behind Berlin instead of 6. Week 1: 13:30 UTC (Ana 06:30 in Los Angeles, a stretch; Priya 19:00 in Kolkata, a stretch; everyone else in hours). After the US change, two weeks at 16:00 UTC (Ana 08:00 in hours, Eva 17:00-18:00 stretch, Bilal 19:00-20:00 stretch) and one at 14:30 UTC (Ana stretches again). Bilal is blocked on 29 October (Republic Day). Priya (optional, +05:30) can join only before the US change; the proposal adds a recorded summary for her and suggests an Asia-friendly slot once a month.

## Rules

- Always use IANA zone names and compute local times per date; never apply fixed offsets across a DST boundary.
- Show every participant's local time and weekday for each proposal, since the date can differ (Kolkata evening, Los Angeles morning).
- Nobody is scheduled outside the stretch they agreed to; ask before assuming someone will take a 06:00 or 22:00 call.
- Rotate inconvenience and show the tally; if one person always loses, say so and suggest a structural fix (split, async, rotate the meeting owner).
- Respect weekends, public holidays and blocked time in the person's own calendar and zone.
- Keep the recommendation short; put the full table in an appendix.

# DST and time zone pitfalls

## Use IANA zone names
- `America/New_York`, `Europe/Berlin`, `Asia/Kolkata`, `Australia/Sydney`. They carry the full history and future rules of that region.
- Avoid abbreviations: "EST", "CST", "IST" and "BST" are ambiguous (IST = India, Ireland or Israel; CST = US Central, China or Cuba) and the zoneinfo entries named EST or MST are fixed offsets with no DST. The script warns on names without a "/".
- Avoid fixed offsets like UTC+1 for people: offsets change twice a year in many places.
- Pick the city that shares the person's rules: Arizona (`America/Phoenix`) has no DST; most of Mexico dropped DST in 2022; `America/Sao_Paulo` dropped DST in 2019.
- Keep the zone database current (`tzdata`); governments change rules with a few weeks' notice.

## DST dates (2026, check each year)
| Region | Summer time starts | Ends | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| US and Canada (most) | 2nd Sunday of March (2026-03-08) | 1st Sunday of November (2026-11-01) | local 02:00 |
| EU, UK | last Sunday of March (2026-03-29) | last Sunday of October (2026-10-25) | 01:00 UTC, all at once |
| Australia (south-east), New Zealand | first Sunday of October / last Sunday of September | first Sunday of April | southern hemisphere: opposite season |
| No DST | Turkey (UTC+3), India (+05:30), China, Japan, Singapore, UAE, most of Africa, Arizona | | |

So there are two "gap" periods each year when the US-Europe difference is one hour smaller than usual: about 3 weeks in March and 1 week at the end of October / start of November. Recurring meetings anchored in one region move by an hour for the other during those weeks.

## Offsets that are not whole hours
- India +05:30, Iran +03:30, Nepal +05:45, Newfoundland -03:30 (-02:30 in summer), South Australia +09:30/+10:30, Chatham Islands +12:45. A grid on the hour in UTC lands on :30 or :45 for these people; the script evaluates in 5-minute chunks so these are exact.

## Weekends and working days
- Sun-Thu working weeks: e.g. Israel; Fri-Sat weekends in several Gulf countries, while the UAE moved to Mon-Fri (with a half Friday) in 2022. Ask each person.
- Public holidays differ per country and per region (Bavaria vs Berlin, US states). Add them to the blocked file in local dates.
- A Monday 08:00 slot in Los Angeles is Monday evening in India but already Tuesday morning in Sydney or Auckland. Always show the weekday per person.

## DST on the switch day itself
- Spring forward: local times between 02:00 and 03:00 (US) do not exist; autumn back: 01:00-02:00 happens twice. Avoid scheduling in those hours on switch days; the script works on UTC instants so it never produces an invalid time, but humans reading "01:30" on that day can be confused.

## Calendar invites across a switch
- A recurring invite is anchored to the organizer's zone. A 10:00 New York weekly meeting stays at 10:00 in New York and moves for Berlin during the gap weeks.
- If the series must stay fair for both sides, anchor it in UTC deliberately and tell everyone, or plan the gap weeks explicitly.
- Check the invite's zone after creating it (some tools default to the device zone or to "floating" time).

# Fairness and rotation

## Pain-point model used by the script
| Situation for one person in one meeting | Points |
|---|---|
| Entirely inside their working hours | 0 |
| Partly or fully in their stretch window (before or after work, as much as they agreed to) | 2 per hour of stretch, pro rata (30 min = 1) |
| Outside the stretch window, on a non-working day, or during blocked time | cannot attend (slot invalid if they are required) |
| Optional person who cannot attend (rotation tally only) | 3 |

Ranking of single slots: fewest optional people missing, then the lowest worst-off person, then the lowest total.

Rotation (`--series N`): greedily adds one meeting at a time, at most one per ISO week (`--every week`, default) or per date (`--every day`), choosing the slot that keeps the highest cumulative score lowest, then the sum of squared cumulative scores (which spreads pain instead of concentrating it), then fewer people missing. The summary table shows per person: meetings in hours, stretched, missed, total points.

The weights are a model, not a truth. Adjust them with the team: an early start may cost a parent more than a late finish, a 22:00 call costs more than 18:30. Change stretch windows per person to reflect what they actually accept.

## Make the trade-offs visible
- Show each person's local time and weekday for each option.
- Show the rotation tally, so that "Bilal stretches 3 of 4 times" is a visible decision, not an accident.
- Ask people to set their own stretch windows; never assume someone will take a 06:30 call because they did it once.

## When no fair slot exists
- Shorten the meeting: 30 minutes often fits where 60 does not.
- Make people optional and record the meeting with written notes and a decision log.
- Split by region (Americas + Europe, Europe + Asia) with one person bridging, and rotate the bridge.
- Alternate two time slots week by week (e.g. 14:00 UTC and 07:00 UTC) so each side gets the convenient one half the time.
- Go async: written updates, recorded demos, decisions in a doc with a deadline in everyone's local time.

## Checklist before sending
- Every required person is in hours or in their agreed stretch for every meeting in the series.
- Holidays and leave in each country are in the blocked file.
- DST changes in the range are named, and the series accounts for them.
- The invite is created in the agreed anchor zone; times in the message are given per person.
- There is a review date (e.g. after the next DST change) to rotate again.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Time zone meeting slot finder (Python 3.9+ standard library: zoneinfo).

Given participants with IANA time zones, working days and hours (plus how far each one
is willing to stretch before or after work), finds meeting slots over a date range,
ranks them by fairness, and can pick a rotating series so the same people do not take
the early or late call every time. Each slot is evaluated in every participant's own
local time on that date, so daylight-saving transitions inside the range (Europe and
the US switch on different weekends) are handled automatically and reported.

Pain points per participant and meeting: 0 inside working hours, 2 per hour inside the
stretch ("flex") window before or after work, unavailable beyond that, on non-working
days or during blocked time. Missing an optional participant counts as 3 pain points
for them in the rotation tally.

Usage:
  python3 slot_finder.py --team team.csv --start 2026-10-26 --end 2026-11-06
        [--duration 60] [--step 30] [--blocked blocked.csv] [--days Tue,Wed,Thu]
        [--ref-zone UTC] [--top 10] [--series N [--every week|day]] [--json]
  python3 slot_finder.py --self-test
team.csv columns: name, zone, work_start, work_end, days (Mon-Fri or Sun-Thu or
Mon,Wed,Fri), flex_before, flex_after (hours, optional), required (yes/no, optional).
work_end earlier than work_start means a shift that runs past midnight.
blocked.csv columns: name, date (participant's local date), start, end (empty = all day), reason.
Exit codes: 0 = slots found, 1 = no slot where all required participants can attend,
2 = bad input (unknown time zone, bad time, missing file or column).
"""
import argparse, csv, datetime as dt, io, json, sys
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo, ZoneInfoNotFoundError

DAY_NAMES = ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"]
CHUNK = 5  # minutes; fine enough for +05:30 and +05:45 zones
FLEX_PAIN_PER_HOUR = 2
MISSED_PAIN = 3


class InputError(Exception):
    pass


def parse_days(s):
    s = (s or "Mon-Fri").strip()
    out = set()
    for part in s.replace(" ", "").split(","):
        if not part:
            continue
        if "-" in part:
            a, b = part.split("-", 1)
            i, j = day_index(a), day_index(b)
            k = i
            while True:
                out.add(k)
                if k == j:
                    break
                k = (k + 1) % 7
        else:
            out.add(day_index(part))
    return out


def day_index(name):
    n = name.strip()[:3].title()
    if n not in DAY_NAMES:
        raise InputError(f"unknown day '{name}' (use Mon..Sun)")
    return DAY_NAMES.index(n)


def parse_hm(s, what):
    try:
        h, m = s.strip().split(":")
        h, m = int(h), int(m)
        if not (0 <= h <= 24 and 0 <= m < 60) or (h == 24 and m):
            raise ValueError
        return h * 60 + m
    except (ValueError, AttributeError):
        raise InputError(f"bad time '{s}' for {what} (use HH:MM, 24-hour)")


def load_zone(name, who, warnings):
    name = (name or "").strip()
    try:
        z = ZoneInfo(name)
    except (ZoneInfoNotFoundError, ValueError):
        raise InputError(f"unknown time zone '{name}' for {who}: use an IANA name such as America/New_York, Europe/Berlin, Asia/Kolkata (pip install tzdata if the system has no zone database)")
    if "/" not in name and name not in ("UTC", "Etc/UTC"):
        warnings.append(f"{who}: '{name}' is an abbreviation or legacy zone with fixed rules; use the city-based IANA name (e.g. America/New_York, not EST) so daylight saving is right")
    return z


def read_team(text, warnings):
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(text.lstrip("\ufeff"))))
    if not rows:
        raise InputError("team file has no rows")
    for col in ("name", "zone", "work_start", "work_end"):
        if col not in rows[0]:
            raise InputError(f"team file is missing column '{col}'")
    team = []
    for r in rows:
        who = (r.get("name") or "").strip()
        if not who:
            continue
        p = {"name": who, "zone_name": r["zone"].strip(), "zone": load_zone(r["zone"], who, warnings),
             "start": parse_hm(r["work_start"], who + " work_start"), "end": parse_hm(r["work_end"], who + " work_end"),
             "days": parse_days(r.get("days")),
             "flex_before": int(round(float(r.get("flex_before") or 0) * 60)),
             "flex_after": int(round(float(r.get("flex_after") or 0) * 60)),
             "required": (r.get("required") or "yes").strip().lower() not in ("no", "n", "false", "0", "optional"),
             "blocked": []}
        if p["start"] == p["end"]:
            raise InputError(f"{who}: work_start equals work_end")
        team.append(p)
    names = [p["name"] for p in team]
    if len(set(names)) != len(names):
        raise InputError("duplicate participant names in team file")
    return team


def read_blocked(text, team):
    byname = {p["name"].lower(): p for p in team}
    for r in csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(text.lstrip("\ufeff"))):
        who = (r.get("name") or "").strip()
        if not who:
            continue
        p = byname.get(who.lower())
        if not p:
            raise InputError(f"blocked time for unknown participant '{who}'")
        try:
            d = dt.date.fromisoformat(r["date"].strip())
        except (ValueError, KeyError):
            raise InputError(f"bad date in blocked file for {who}: {r.get('date')}")
        s, e = (r.get("start") or "").strip(), (r.get("end") or "").strip()
        a = dt.datetime.combine(d, dt.time()) + dt.timedelta(minutes=parse_hm(s, who + " blocked start") if s else 0)
        b = dt.datetime.combine(d, dt.time()) + dt.timedelta(minutes=parse_hm(e, who + " blocked end") if e else 1440)
        p["blocked"].append((a, b, (r.get("reason") or "").strip()))


def classify(p, local):
    """local: naive local datetime. Return 'core', 'flex' or None (unavailable)."""
    best = None
    for back in (0, 1):
        d = local.date() - dt.timedelta(days=back)
        if d.weekday() not in p["days"]:
            continue
        base = dt.datetime.combine(d, dt.time())
        cs = base + dt.timedelta(minutes=p["start"])
        ce = base + dt.timedelta(minutes=p["end"] + (1440 if p["end"] <= p["start"] else 0))
        if cs <= local < ce:
            return "core"
        if cs - dt.timedelta(minutes=p["flex_before"]) <= local < ce + dt.timedelta(minutes=p["flex_after"]):
            best = "flex"
    return best


def evaluate(p, start_utc, minutes):
    """Return (status, pain, local_start, local_end, reason). status in core, flex, out."""
    flex_min = 0
    reason = ""
    for k in range(0, minutes, CHUNK):
        t = (start_utc + dt.timedelta(minutes=k)).astimezone(p["zone"]).replace(tzinfo=None)
        c = classify(p, t)
        if c is None:
            reason = "outside hours" if t.date().weekday() in p["days"] or classify_day_any(p, t) else "day off"
            return "out", 0.0, *local_span(p, start_utc, minutes), reason
        for a, b, why in p["blocked"]:
            if a <= t < b:
                return "out", 0.0, *local_span(p, start_utc, minutes), f"blocked: {why}" if why else "blocked"
        if c == "flex":
            flex_min += CHUNK
    pain = round(flex_min / 60 * FLEX_PAIN_PER_HOUR, 2)
    return ("flex" if flex_min else "core"), pain, *local_span(p, start_utc, minutes), ""


def classify_day_any(p, t):
    return (t.date() - dt.timedelta(days=1)).weekday() in p["days"] and p["end"] <= p["start"]


def local_span(p, start_utc, minutes):
    a = start_utc.astimezone(p["zone"])
    b = (start_utc + dt.timedelta(minutes=minutes)).astimezone(p["zone"])
    return a, b


def dst_changes(team, start, end):
    out = []
    seen = set()
    for p in team:
        if p["zone_name"] in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(p["zone_name"])
        z = p["zone"]
        t = dt.datetime.combine(start - dt.timedelta(days=1), dt.time(), tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc)
        stop = dt.datetime.combine(end + dt.timedelta(days=2), dt.time(), tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc)
        prev = t.astimezone(z).utcoffset()
        while t < stop:
            t2 = t + dt.timedelta(minutes=30)
            off = t2.astimezone(z).utcoffset()
            if off != prev:
                loc = t2.astimezone(z)
                out.append({"zone": p["zone_name"], "utc": t2.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC"),
                            "local": loc.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M %Z"), "from": fmt_off(prev), "to": fmt_off(off)})
                prev = off
            t = t2
    return out


def fmt_off(td):
    m = int(td.total_seconds() // 60)
    s = "+" if m >= 0 else "-"
    m = abs(m)
    return f"UTC{s}{m // 60:02d}:{m % 60:02d}"


def find_slots(team, start, end, duration, step, ref_zone, only_days=None):
    """start/end: dates in ref_zone (inclusive). Returns list of slot dicts."""
    slots = []
    t = dt.datetime.combine(start, dt.time(), tzinfo=ref_zone).astimezone(dt.timezone.utc)
    stop = dt.datetime.combine(end + dt.timedelta(days=1), dt.time(), tzinfo=ref_zone).astimezone(dt.timezone.utc)
    t = t.replace(minute=(t.minute // step) * step if step < 60 else 0, second=0, microsecond=0)
    while t + dt.timedelta(minutes=duration) <= stop:
        ref_local = t.astimezone(ref_zone)
        if only_days is None or ref_local.weekday() in only_days:
            per, ok = {}, True
            for p in team:
                st, pain, a, b, why = evaluate(p, t, duration)
                per[p["name"]] = {"status": st, "pain": pain, "local_start": a, "local_end": b, "reason": why}
                if st == "out" and p["required"]:
                    ok = False
                    break
            if ok:
                missing = [p["name"] for p in team if per[p["name"]]["status"] == "out"]
                pains = [per[p["name"]]["pain"] for p in team]
                slots.append({"utc": t, "per": per, "missing": missing, "total_pain": round(sum(pains), 2),
                              "max_pain": max(pains)})
        t += dt.timedelta(minutes=step)
    return slots


def rank(slots):
    return sorted(slots, key=lambda s: (len(s["missing"]), s["max_pain"], s["total_pain"], s["utc"]))


def period_key(s, ref_zone, every):
    d = s["utc"].astimezone(ref_zone).date()
    return d.isocalendar()[:2] if every == "week" else d


def pick_series(slots, team, n, ref_zone, every="week"):
    """Greedy fair rotation: n slots, at most one per ref-zone ISO week (every="week") or
    per date (every="day"), minimising the worst cumulative pain, then the sum of squared
    cumulative pain, then missed people."""
    cum = {p["name"]: 0.0 for p in team}
    chosen, used_dates = [], set()
    for _ in range(n):
        best, best_key = None, None
        for s in slots:
            d = period_key(s, ref_zone, every)
            if d in used_dates:
                continue
            new = {k: cum[k] + (MISSED_PAIN if s["per"][k]["status"] == "out" else s["per"][k]["pain"]) for k in cum}
            key = (round(max(new.values()), 2), round(sum(v * v for v in new.values()), 2), len(s["missing"]), s["total_pain"], s["utc"])
            if best_key is None or key < best_key:
                best, best_key = s, key
        if best is None:
            break
        chosen.append(best)
        used_dates.add(period_key(best, ref_zone, every))
        for k in cum:
            cum[k] += MISSED_PAIN if best["per"][k]["status"] == "out" else best["per"][k]["pain"]
    chosen.sort(key=lambda s: s["utc"])
    return chosen, cum


def cell(info):
    a, b = info["local_start"], info["local_end"]
    txt = f"{DAY_NAMES[a.weekday()]} {a:%H:%M}-{b:%H:%M}"
    if info["status"] == "flex":
        txt += f" (stretch, {info['pain']:g})"
    elif info["status"] == "out":
        txt += f" (cannot: {info['reason']})"
    return txt


def table(slots, team, ref_zone):
    head = ["#", f"Start ({ref_zone.key})"] + [f"{p['name']} ({p['zone_name']})" for p in team] + ["Pain total/max", "Missing"]
    out = ["| " + " | ".join(head) + " |", "|" + "---|" * len(head)]
    for i, s in enumerate(slots, 1):
        r = s["utc"].astimezone(ref_zone)
        row = [str(i), f"{DAY_NAMES[r.weekday()]} {r:%Y-%m-%d %H:%M}"] + [cell(s["per"][p["name"]]) for p in team] + \
              [f"{s['total_pain']:g}/{s['max_pain']:g}", ", ".join(s["missing"]) or "-"]
        out.append("| " + " | ".join(row) + " |")
    return out


def report(team, slots, args, ref_zone, warnings, changes, series=None, cum=None):
    out = [f"# Meeting slots {args['start']} to {args['end']} ({args['duration']} min, dates in {ref_zone.key})", ""]
    for w in warnings:
        out.append(f"> WARNING: {w}")
    if warnings:
        out.append("")
    out.append("## Participants")
    out.append("| Name | Zone | Hours (local) | Days | Stretch before/after | Required |")
    out.append("|---|---|---|---|---|---|")
    for p in team:
        days = ",".join(DAY_NAMES[d] for d in sorted(p["days"]))
        out.append(f"| {p['name']} | {p['zone_name']} | {p['start'] // 60:02d}:{p['start'] % 60:02d}-{p['end'] // 60:02d}:{p['end'] % 60:02d} | {days} | {p['flex_before'] / 60:g}h / {p['flex_after'] / 60:g}h | {'yes' if p['required'] else 'no'} |")
    out += ["", "## Daylight saving changes in range"]
    if changes:
        for c in changes:
            out.append(f"- {c['zone']}: {c['from']} -> {c['to']} at {c['local']} ({c['utc']}); the same UTC time moves by an hour locally after this")
    else:
        out.append("- none")
    out.append("")
    if not slots:
        out.append("No slot found where every required participant is available. Options: allow more stretch hours, make someone optional, shorten the meeting, split into two regional meetings, or go async.")
        return "\n".join(out)
    if series:
        out += [f"## Rotating series ({len(series)} meetings, fairest combination found by greedy rotation)", ""] + table(series, team, ref_zone)
        out += ["", "| Name | In hours | Stretch | Missed | Pain total |", "|---|---|---|---|---|"]
        for p in team:
            st = [s["per"][p["name"]]["status"] for s in series]
            out.append(f"| {p['name']} | {st.count('core')} | {st.count('flex')} | {st.count('out')} | {cum[p['name']]:g} |")
        out.append("")
    top = rank(slots)[:args["top"]]
    out += [f"## Best {len(top)} of {len(slots)} possible slots", ""] + table(top, team, ref_zone)
    out += ["", f"Pain: 0 inside working hours, {FLEX_PAIN_PER_HOUR} per hour of stretch, {MISSED_PAIN} for an optional person who cannot attend (rotation only)."]
    return "\n".join(out)


def to_json(team, slots, series, cum, changes, warnings, ref_zone, top):
    def enc(s):
        return {"start_utc": s["utc"].strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%MZ"), "start_ref": s["utc"].astimezone(ref_zone).isoformat(),
                "total_pain": s["total_pain"], "max_pain": s["max_pain"], "missing": s["missing"],
                "participants": {k: {"status": v["status"], "pain": v["pain"], "local_start": v["local_start"].isoformat(),
                                     "local_end": v["local_end"].isoformat(), "reason": v["reason"]} for k, v in s["per"].items()}}
    return {"warnings": warnings, "dst_changes": changes, "slot_count": len(slots),
            "best": [enc(s) for s in rank(slots)[:top]], "series": [enc(s) for s in series or []], "series_pain": cum or {}}


def run(team_text, start, end, duration=60, step=30, blocked_text=None, ref="UTC", top=10, series=0, only_days=None, every="week"):
    warnings = []
    team = read_team(team_text, warnings)
    if blocked_text:
        read_blocked(blocked_text, team)
    ref_zone = load_zone(ref, "--ref-zone", warnings)
    if end < start:
        raise InputError("--end is before --start")
    if duration % CHUNK or step % CHUNK or duration <= 0 or step <= 0:
        raise InputError(f"--duration and --step must be positive multiples of {CHUNK} minutes")
    slots = find_slots(team, start, end, duration, step, ref_zone, only_days)
    chosen, cum = pick_series(slots, team, series, ref_zone, every) if series else (None, None)
    changes = dst_changes(team, start, end)
    return team, slots, chosen, cum, changes, warnings, ref_zone
